messages:
rachel_perf: noticing a cluster of P95/P99 spikes on host ingress after the new kernel-routing tweak (rolled at 02:30). Mostly streaming-heavy traffic. Dash: https://dash.redwood/ingress/hosts/streams/999

sam_runtime: thanks, which tweak specifically? the selector change that prefers low-latency kernels for short seqs?

rachel_perf: yep that one (PR#4201). Correlation matrix points to more small-write syscalls during response streaming and higher parse latency for multilingual inputs.

teeq_infra: I pulled an strace from a stressed Dedicated pod. snippet:
```
writev(1, [{iov_base="\x00...", iov_len=128}, {iov_base="\x01...", iov_len=64}], 2) = 192
writev(1, [{iov_base="\x02...", iov_len=32}], 1) = 32
-- repeated ~40x per request --
```
shows increased fragmentation vs baseline which had more coalesced larger writev calls.

ana_sre: also seeing a small but consistent uptick in KV evictions (2.3% extra) around the same windows. Could be because prefix boundaries changed and cache keys no longer match.

rachel_perf: ran a 60s microbenchmark comparing kernel routing options. numbers (median ms):
- baseline (throughput kernel): tokenize+parse = 2.3ms, writev-count/request = 4
- new selector (auto -> low-latency): tokenize+parse = 3.9ms, writev-count/request = 18
So >60% parse hit and ~4x syscall churn. Details in gist: https://gist.redwood/bench/999

sam_runtime: wow. kernel heuristic appears to flip a flag that disables our prefix-merge fastpath in preparse. That's likely why writev count explodes. Any hypothesis on why selector chose low-latency more often?

teeq_infra: selector uses sequence length distribution + recent tail latency. During last canary subset we had a spike of short-chat requests which biased the per-host score. rollout percentage increases then made the heuristic affect more hosts.

ana_sre: mitigation options? we can't revert full thing without losing some low-latency wins for tiny requests. Maybe make the selector aware of tokenizer-cost impact.

rachel_perf: proposed plan:
- short term: add a runtime guard that preserves prefix-merge if request contains mixed-script or emoji sequences (heuristic: emoji_ratio > 0.05 or non-ascii-run-length > 8)
- telemetry: emit `writev_count`, `tokenizer_path` tag, `kernel_variant` per-request
- long term: modify kernel-selector to compute a delta-cost estimate = tokenizer_penalty + syscall_penalty and prefer throughput kernel when delta > threshold

sam_runtime: agree. also add a small e2e microbench to CI that runs mixed-language tokenization + streaming to catch regressions.

teeq_infra: I'll drop a short-term feature-flagged patch to preserve prefix-merge when `preserve_coalesce=true` is set at host-level. Canary that to 10% and watch writev_count metrics.

rachel_perf: can we also instrument the http2 framer to report frame coalescing ratio? would help quantify writev -> network framing overhead.

ana_sre: creating a dashboard: `ingress/host/writev_per_request`, `ingress/host/frame_coalesce_ratio`, `kv/hitrate_by_prefix_shape`. Will pin alerts for >30% increase.

deploy-bot: patch (ff: preserve-prefix-merge) scheduled to canary at 2026-03-23T12:45:00Z (deploy-id: dpl-8002).

sam_runtime: owners: rachel -> perf validation & bench, teeq -> patch + canary, ana -> dashboards/alerts. Target: canary validate within 2h and then gradual roll if green.

rachel_perf: I'll run a longer 5m flame and attach before/after to the PR. If we can show writev_count drop and KV hit recover, we can accept a conservative selector tweak.

ana_sre: one more thing: add gating test for tokenization shapes (include emoji-heavy and CJK samples). We've been missing that in selector coverage.

sam_runtime: noted. thanks team. meeting 12:30 to review canary telemetry. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
